elements.name: Zinc
elements.fact: Zinc coats steel to stop it rusting (galvanising). It reacts steadily with acids, giving off hydrogen.

elements.name: Tin
elements.fact: A bar of tin "cries": it crackles when bent as its crystals slide past each other.

elements.name: Lead
elements.fact: Lead is soft, heavy and poisonous. Romans used it for water pipes, which is where the word plumbing comes from (plumbum).

elements.name: Nickel
elements.fact: Nickel is magnetic, like iron and cobalt.

elements.name: Silver
elements.fact: Silver conducts heat and electricity better than any other metal.

elements.name: Manganese
elements.fact: Manganese makes steel tough. Its compounds come in pink, green and deep purple.

elements.name: Chromium
elements.fact: Chromium gives stainless steel its shine and its resistance to rust.

elements.name: Cobalt
elements.fact: Cobalt compounds give glass and pottery their deep blue.

elements.name: Barium
elements.fact: Barium burns with an apple-green flame, used in green fireworks.

elements.name: Platinum
elements.fact: Platinum is a superb catalyst: ammonia and oxygen burn on a red-hot platinum gauze to make nitric oxide, the first step to nitric acid.

elements.name: Bismuth
elements.fact: Bismuth grows into rainbow-coloured staircase crystals when it cools from a melt.

elements.name: Strontium
elements.fact: Strontium burns crimson red: it is the red in fireworks and flares.
